thread:
Elena: Quick sync — Windward pilot blocked. They cant get the Rust SDK + SSE handshake to do function-calls with our structured output. Asking for a short workaround and pricing + security checklist.
Sam: Rust SDK supports SSE streaming but function-calling is experimental in Rust client. We recommend edge-proxy shim as a pragmatic fallback.
Sam: Minimal sketch of the shim behavior:
```rust
// pseudo-code
let mut s = client.stream(req).await?;
while let Some(chunk) = s.next().await {
  if chunk.contains_toolcall() {
    // convert to internal webhook / forward to tool service
  } else {
    // forward tokens to consumer
  }
}
```
Elena: Can SEs share that snippet + a small example repo? Windward infra wants something they can run locally in 30m.
Sam: Ill slap together a tiny repo and include a docker-compose with an edge-proxy container. Will post link here.
Priya: Procurement ping — they want hosted vs 12-month Dedicated compare for ~100 RPS sustained streaming @ ~1.2k tokens/req. Can we give a one-pager ballpark?
Ben: Quick ballpark: hosted gen tier ~ $0.00075-0.0009 per token depending on model. For 100 RPS @1.2k tokens = 120k tokens/sec -> ~10.4B tokens/day, which is big. Dedicated (1x A100-class reserved) is likely cheaper at scale; estimate depends on model & quant. Ill produce a hosted vs Dedicated TCO sample with a few model/quant scenarios.
Priya: Please include assumptions (model size, tokenization, average response length, prefix caching hit-rate) so procurement can compare apples-to-apples.
Ben: Will do. Also note egress and private deployment fees.
Elena: Security questionnaire highlights: KMS integration, SSO (SAML), audit log retention, and whether we support cert pinning for on-prem connectors.
Ben: We have docs: SOC2 attestation, enterprise KMS integration guide, SAML SSO guide. Ill extract the relevant snippets into a short checklist and mark anything that needs legal sign-off.
ops-bot: Created ticket WD-4219 for on-prem credentialing + runbook handoff (assignee: Elena).
Sam: Short-term dev plan: Windward runs their Rust client unchanged; we run edge-proxy in their DMZ to terminate SSE & translate function-calls into a webhook format their connector already understands. Config example for proxy:
```
edge_proxy:
  listener: 0.0.0.0:443
  mode: sse
  forward_toolcalls: true
  webhook_endpoint: http://localhost:8080/tool-handler
  tls: terminate
```
This avoids touching their onprem binary until Rust client function-call GA.
Elena: They also want our structured-output JSON spec + a few sample payloads to validate against their ingestion pipeline.
Sam: Example payload (tool response): {\"tool\": \"extract_entities\", \"result\": {\"entities\": [{\"type\":\"PERSON\",\"text\":\"Alex\"}]}}. Ill include a couple of larger-ish examples in the repo.
Priya: Timeline ask from Windward: demo of workaround + pricing one-pager by EOD tomorrow. Can we hit that?
Ben: Draft pricing one-pager today, final after model choice tomorrow.
Sam: Repo + proxy config by EOD today.
Elena: Great. Plan: Sam = sample repo + proxy config, Ben = security checklist + pricing draft, Priya = one-pager for procurement. Ill consolidate and send to Windward with proposed call times.
Priya: I can join the call with their infra folks if needed.
Elena: Thanks—I'll file the handoff and include the ticket WD-4219. :thumbsup:
